text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (28.6%, 2.1%, 13.44, 4.45, 64%, 29 records, 8 documented 99215 with 0 below billed). The leaning is appropriately cautious. However, several claims are not grounded in the card, and the narrative contradicts itself. The next steps are weaker than the rationale text suggests.","problems":["Claims C0035237 is a 'rash' and C0035241 an 'upper respiratory infection', but the card gives only dx codes R21 and J06.9 with no descriptions; R21 is rash, J06.9 is URI, so this is an inference presented as fact.","Claims C0035293 is a 'problems-flagged note' and is in the documented set, but the card has no per-claim note flags; the card lists C0035293 only as a 0-condition 99215 (R10.9) and does not show it as documented.","Refers to 'documented minutes cluster tightly (46-54) with a notable time-repeat rate' and 'nearly half the notes carry the problems signal'. The card shows only four example minutes, and no time-repeat rate or problems share; these come from unverified sources.","Speculates that documentation 'may be inflated' and about templated or cloned notes with little evidence, which undercuts the finding that all 8 documented 99215 claims were supported.","Next steps are inconsistent: the rationale says start with C0035293, while the next-steps list starts with C0035231 and C0035237; the rationale also asks for charts and the audit trail but the next steps do not mention the audit trail.","Does not note that low-complexity 99215 claims were not among those with returned records, so documentation cannot speak to them; the point is implied but not stated clearly.","Cites only two claims, both low-complexity, and none of the supported documented claims it mentions (C0035389, C0035465) in the cited list."]}
